title: Model-Informed Gold Revisions Inflate Measured Accuracy: A Versioned Gold-Standard Protocol for LLM Extraction of ESG Data
abstract: Language-model extraction of ESG data is scored against human references that are often revised after the model has run, yet those revisions are seldom versioned or measured. We propose a versioned gold-standard protocol: a blind reference fixed before extraction, every later revision logged with its page evidence and trigger, identical predictions scored against every version, and a worst-case headline. We apply it to 36 stratified Hang Seng Index constituents (396 cells, eleven headline fields). Revisions prompted by model disagreement change 22 cells, 21 toward the model, and raise measured accuracy by 5.1 percentage points with the predictions unchanged. Against the blind reference, a BM25-plus-LLM pipeline scores 90.9% (firm-bootstrap 95% CI 87.1-93.9%) on the 24 firms annotated fully blind and never used in prompt development, and 90.7% on all 36 (89.6% under the pre-specified unit normaliser). A generic regex-and-table heuristic scores 35.6%. Retrieval placed the gold evidence page in the model's context for 98% of disclosed cells, including every missed or wrong value that has a cited page. Under the written prompt, only two of the 37 errors are model errors, plus one masked by an identical gold error. The rest are gold omissions, prompt-gold specification conflicts, definitional ambiguity and unverifiable disclosure. For this reasoning model, residual error arises after retrieval, in the definition of the target; a partial comparison suggests a weaker model loses about ten points. ESG extraction accuracy is a property of a model and a reference together, and benchmarks should report both.

title: Cost-Quality Frontiers in LLM-Assisted Policy Analysis: Multi-Model Consensus for Structured Extraction and Evaluative Scoring
abstract: <span>We present an open instrumentation suite for AI-assisted policy analysis that combines dual analysis pipelines, multi-model consensus, human-in-the-loop review, and perrequest observability in a single, domain-agnostic platform. The system implements two complementary pipelines: gap detection (framework → policy) and fit scoring (policy → framework), enabling systematic assessment of whether a jurisdiction’s policies cover a reference framework and how well. Read across jurisdictions, the same fit matrices invert the question, measuring whether the framework itself fits the policy reality it is meant to track. We instantiate the platform on four National Adaptation Plans evaluated against the Belém Adaptation Indicators (COP30) and compare six extraction models spanning four cost tiers, from free local models to premium APIs, using multi-model majority-vote consensus as pseudo-ground-truth. Key findings: (i) DeepSeek V4 Flash achieves F₁ = 0.937 at $0.04 per document, matching premium models at ~28x lower cost; (ii) precision-recall profiles diverge sharply across models, with no single model dominating all documents; (iii) inter-coder reliability between two independent scoring judges (Krippendorff’s α = 0.488) reveals that evaluative scoring is substantially harder than extraction; and (iv) free-tier models (Qwen 3.6 35B local, Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite cloud) achieve competitive extraction quality (F₁ ≥ 0.873), demonstrating that cost need not be a barrier to multi-model policy analysis. The platform’s domain-agnostic design enables application to any structured policy evaluation task (SDG reporting, TCFD compliance, CRPD mapping) without code changes.</span><span></span>

title: Analyzing Model Extraction Vulnerabilities in Commercial Security AI Services
abstract: The widespread integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into commercial security services—encompassing threat detection, fraud prevention, and physical surveillance—introduces a critical yet often overlooked attack vector: model extraction. In this paradigm, adversaries can systematically query a black-box security AI service and use the observed input-output pairs to reconstruct a functionally equivalent or superior surrogate model. This research investigates the unique vulnerabilities of commercial security AI to extraction attacks, differentiating them from extraction in other domains due to the inherent asymmetries of security data. Unlike standard AI services, security models operate on adversarial distributions characterized by high class imbalance, concept drift, and the constant evolution of attack patterns. We first formalize a threat model tailored to security AI, outlining adversary capabilities and objectives, from stealing a detection algorithm to creating evasion samples. We then conduct a comprehensive empirical analysis of leading commercial security APIs, employing state-of-the-art extraction techniques such as query-efficient active learning and generative adversarial network (GAN)-based synthesis. Our findings reveal a profound "extraction-paradox": the very mechanisms designed to bolster security—such as uncertainty sampling or differential privacy in model updates—can inadvertently be reverse-engineered to enhance the fidelity of the stolen model. Furthermore, we demonstrate that extracted models are not merely intellectual property violations but potent tools for crafting highly effective adversarial examples, enabling a cascade of attacks including targeted misclassification and evasion that bypasses the original service's defenses. To counter this threat, we propose and evaluate a suite of defensive strategies, including adaptive query filtering, output perturbation, and the strategic introduction of decoy "honeypot" predictions. Our results underscore that current commercial security AI services are dangerously susceptible to extraction, and we conclude by outlining a pragmatic roadmap for developing robust, extraction-resistant AI systems, emphasizing the need for security-by-design principles rather than post-deployment patches.

title: IAGD: An LLM-Guided Implicit-Augmented Graph Diffusion Model for Aspect Sentiment Triplet Extraction
authors: Chang Zhang; Yuan Zhang; fengzhou sun; GuoQiang Zhang
abstract: Aspect Sentiment Triplet Extraction (ASTE) aims to jointly identify aspect targets, opinion expressions, and sentiment polarities. However, real-world ASTE faces two severe challenges: semantic deficiencies from implicit expressions, and complex long-range dependencies caused by interwoven explicit and implicit features. To this end, this paper proposes a sentiment analysis model based on Implicit-Augmented Graph Diffusion (IAGD), constructing a dual-driven collaborative paradigm of &apos;&apos;knowledge guidance and structural reasoning&apos;&apos;. At the knowledge level, it utilizes Large Language Model (LLM) as an offline reasoning engine to generate implicit semantic cues, injecting them into the feature space as soft prompts to fill the semantic gaps. At the structural level, it constructs a multi-view heterogeneous graph integrating semantic, syntactic, and positional features, and designs an adaptive multi-relational graph diffusion algorithm. Through a sparse mixed diffusion mechanism, this algorithm effectively mitigates the over-smoothing problem of deep graph networks while precisely capturing explicit and implicit logical associations over long distances. Experiments on the DMASTE and multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that IAGD achieves state-of-the-art performance, significantly enhancing the end-to-end extraction capability of fine-grained sentiment elements in complex contexts.

title: LLM-CG: Large language model-enhanced constraint graph for distantly supervised relation extraction
Large Language Model (LLM)-Based Automation for Software Test Script Generation
abstract: With the rapid evolution of software systems and the growing complexity of their testing needs, test automation has become more essential than ever within the software development life cycle (SDLC). Yet, despite advances in tooling, the process of creating test scripts still tends to be manual, time-consuming, and highly dependent on both programming skills and domain expertise. In this study, we explore a practical approach that uses Large Language Models (LLMs) including GPT-based models to automate the generation of test scripts directly from natural language software requirements or user stories. The method combines prompt engineering with lightweight fine-tuning and the use of domain-specific data to generate executable test cases. We applied this framework across a range of real-world software projects and used popular testing tools like Selenium and PyTest to assess performance in terms of script accuracy, maintainability, and the overall reduction in developer workload. Our findings show that LLM-generated tests significantly reduce manual effort and produce results that are close to human-written scripts in terms of coverage and correctness. Overall, the approach offers a flexible solution for integrating AI-powered test generation into CI/CD pipelines and could mark a step forward in how teams approach software testing in agile environments.

title: Применение LLM (Large Language Model) на основе комплексного подхода (дообучение + LLM firewall + On-Premise) для обеспечения максимального уровня экономической безопасности и эффективности предприятий молочной промышленности
abstract: В статье проведено исследование особенностей применения LLM (Large Language Model)  на основе комплексного подхода (дообучение + LLM Firewall + On-Premise) для обеспечения максимального уровня экономической безопасности и эффективности предприятий молочной промышленности в современных  условиях. Рассмотрено несколько подходов к интеграции LLM с контролируемой базой знаний в сфере экономической безопасности молочной промышленности, которые позволяют снизить риски и повысить точность работы модели. Разобрано иерархическое соотношение шести программных комплексов – от базовых инфраструктурных решений к высокоуровневым прикладным системам. Показано, что интеграция RAG с LLM трансформирует генеративные модели в стратегический актив экономической безопасности отрасли, сочетающий гибкость ИИ с точностью отраслевой экспертизы и соблюдением требований конфиденциальности данных.                     The article examines the features of the LLM (Large Language Model) application  based on an integrated approach: retraining + LLM Firewall + On-Premise to ensure the maximum level of economic security and efficiency of dairy industry enterprises in modern conditions. Several approaches to integrating LLM with a controlled knowledge base in the field of economic security of the dairy industry are considered, which can reduce risks and improve the accuracy of the model. The hierarchical relationship of six software complexes is analyzed – from basic infrastructure solutions to high-level application systems. It is shown that the integration of RAG with LLM transforms generative models into a strategic asset for the economic security of the industry, combining the flexibility of AI with the accuracy of industry expertise and compliance with data confidentiality requirements.

title: Leveraging an African-Centered Language Model (LLM) for Dismantling White Supremacy: The Case of “SMOKY”
abstract: The system outlined in this proposal exists in a conceptual phase, awaiting the necessary resources for implementation. The theoretical framework presented herein lays the foundation for the development and deployment of 'Smoky,' an innovative artificial intelligence system designed to confront systemic racism. Grounded in African-centered scholarship and equipped with sophisticated monitoring capabilities, 'Smoky' stands as a pioneering endeavor in the realm of leveraging technology for social equity. This scholarly exploration delves into the conceptualization, development, and potential applications of 'Smoky' as a formidable asset in the ongoing struggle against racial injustice. As with any transformative idea, securing funding and support is paramount to transitioning from theory to tangible action. This paper serves as a call to philanthropists and potential collaborators to join in the realization of this vision, contributing to the advancement of technology-driven solutions for social justice.
